candidateOutput.title: Trapping Rain Water
candidateOutput.crux: Given an elevation map, find total units of water trapped between bars after rain.
edgeCases: strictly increasing height → 0 water, no valleys
strictly decreasing height → 0 water, no valleys
height = [5,0,5] → 5 water, bounded by two tall bars
max height at ends → 0 water, water flows out
large plateau at max height → water trapped only between plateaus

wrongApproaches.name: Naive Left-Right Max Precomputation
wrongApproaches.signal: two nested loops scanning left and right for each index
wrongApproaches.reason: O(N^2) time with N up to 2*10^4 causes TLE

wrongApproaches.name: Brute Force Water per Cell
wrongApproaches.signal: for each i, find max left and max right by linear scan
wrongApproaches.reason: repeatedly scans same subarrays, quadratic complexity

wrongApproaches.name: Two Pointers without tracking left_max/right_max
wrongApproaches.signal: move pointer based only on height comparison
wrongApproaches.reason: loses track of bounding max, computes wrong water amount

wrongApproaches.name: Monotonic Stack storing only heights
wrongApproaches.reason: cannot compute width between bars, water amount incorrect

optimal.name: Two Pointers with Left/Right Max Tracking
optimal.keyIdea: Maintain left_max and right pointers moving inward; water at each step bounded by min(left_max, right_max) - height[ptr], move the side with smaller max.
invariants: water added = min(left_max, right_max) - height[ptr] when positive
pointer with smaller bounding max moves inward each iteration
pitfalls: forgetting to update left_max/right_max before computing water
moving the wrong pointer when left_max == right_max (any direction works but must be consistent)
integer overflow not an issue as heights <= 10^5 and n <= 2*10^4, max water <= 2*10^9 fits 32-bit int
recognizeBy: if height[left] < height[right]: process left else process right

alternates.name: Prefix Max + Suffix Max + Sum Difference
alternates.keyIdea: Compute left_max[i] = max height to left of i, right_max[i] = max height to right of i, water[i] = min(left_max[i], right_max[i]) - height[i], sum all water[i].
alternates.whyNotOptimal: O(N) extra space for two arrays vs O(1) two-pointer solution
recognizeBy: for i in 1..n-1: leftMax[i] = max(leftMax[i-1], height[i-1])

alternates.name: Monotonic Decreasing Stack
alternates.keyIdea: Maintain stack of indices with decreasing heights; when a higher bar arrives, pop and compute water trapped between the popped bar, the new bar, and the stack top.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: O(N) stack space; two-pointer uses O(1) space
recognizeBy: while stack not empty and height[i] > height[stack.top()]:

alternates.name: Brute Force Left/Right Max Scan
alternates.keyIdea: For each index i, scan left to find max height, scan right to find max height, add min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i] to total.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Nested loops give O(N^2); N=2*10^4 gives 2*10^8 ops, TLE on LeetCode
recognizeBy: for j in 0..i: maxLeft = max(maxLeft, height[j])
for k in i..n-1: maxRight = max(maxRight, height[k])

alternates.name: Divide and Conquer Recursion
alternates.keyIdea: Recursively split array at global maximum, solve left and right subproblems, combine results.
alternates.time: O(N log N) average, O(N^2) worst case
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Worst-case O(N^2) when array is sorted; recursion overhead vs simple two-pointer

personal.reason: Optimal mechanics identifies Two Pointers O(N) time O(1) space with leftMax and rightMax bounding invariants, matching the rubric.
